title: Crouwel Press — Stedelijk Exhibition Wall
description: A museum-poster title slide ruled by one enormous condensed headline crashing into the top edge and tiny mono dates anchoring the foot — bone paper, nothing else. The single thin rule and cadmium-red meta accent are its only concessions to decoration.
philosophy: This template holds that typography is the only architecture a slide needs. It refuses images, icons, gradients, and decorative ornament because every visual element that is not a letterform is a debt against clarity. It was built for curators, cultural institutions, and designers who want an opening frame that reads like a Stedelijk Museum poster from 1968 — utterly authoritative in its restraint. The speaker who deploys it trusts the word completely; the room it belongs in is silent before the headline lands.
goodFor: Opening title slides for design retrospectives and cultural exhibitions
3-line headline statements where the letterform is the entire visual
Academic conference keynotes with a design-history or art-criticism angle
Brand identity presentations aimed at design-literate or institutional audiences
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring multiple data panels
Slides needing photography, product imagery, or illustration
Pitch decks with bullet-point-dense content across many sections
Audiences expecting warm, approachable, or consumer-friendly aesthetics
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a Stedelijk Museum exhibition poster scaled to fill an architectural wall — the headline does not sit on the page, it lands on it with full weight. Compositional drama is achieved entirely through the collision of enormous letterform mass at the top edge against deep negative space below a single incised rule. The mood is cool institutional authority punctuated by one flash of cadmium warmth in the meta-text accent — restrained but not indifferent. Avoid every softening gesture: no background texture, no tonal graduation, no bounding boxes, no ornamental marks beyond the one structural rule.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-col grid; the condensed headline spans all 12 columns with zero top clearance, letterforms intentionally cropping into the upper slide edge to create typographic collision. A single hairline rule runs full-bleed at approximately 68% of the slide height, cleaving the headline mass from the footer zone. Exhibition subtitle or deck descriptor sits in a narrow band directly above the rule, left-aligned to an 8% inner margin. Mono meta-text — dates, institution name, catalog number — locks flush-left at the very foot of the slide, no bottom padding.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like catalogue wall text at its most authoritative — one dominant typographic statement, condensed and nearly crashing its container, commands the upper zone, held taut by a single thin rule crossing the full measure. Below, supporting text delivers substance in sparse, unornamented lines. The mood is institutional silence: no warmth, no illustration, no decorative concession — only the absolute confidence of dark ink pressed onto bone paper.

  <text x="154" y="430" font-size="298" letter-spacing="-12" textLength="1612" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">FORM IS</text>
  <text x="154" y="660" font-size="298" letter-spacing="-12" textLength="1612" lengthAdjust="spacingAndGlyphs">ARGUMENT.</text>

<!-- Tiny blue annotation in margin, just past the anchor -->

<g font-family="ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif" fill="#1a1a1a">

  <text x="154" y="898" font-size="28" font-weight="400">every margin a refusal. Restraint is the loudest instrument we own.</text>

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with approximately 8% outer margin; primary content sits in cols 2–10. A condensed typographic anchor — oversized key term, stat, or quote fragment — fills the upper zone, followed by a single full-width thin rule bisecting the field. Supporting body text of two to four short lines occupies the lower third directly beneath the rule, with a mono-spaced red accent label flush-left above the anchor as a section identifier. Page number in mono anchors bottom-right; no enclosing header or footer band.
